objective.subject: mathematics
objective.target: Independently add unlike-denominator fractions using equal-sized units, explain why the denominator cannot simply be added, and transfer the method to a new example.
prerequisites: interpret denominator as size/count of equal parts
add quantities in the same units

baseline.studentPrompt: Without assistance, calculate 1/3 + 1/4 and explain the units you are adding.
baseline.referenceAnswer: 7/12; convert to twelfths and add equal-sized fractional units.

immediate.studentPrompt: Without assistance, calculate 2/3 + 1/4 and explain why the denominator is suitable.

nearTransfer.studentPrompt: Without assistance, calculate 3/5 + 1/6 and explain your method.

delayed.studentPrompt: Without assistance, calculate 2/5 + 1/3 and describe how you chose the common units.

pathways.authoredLearnerEvidence: I know how to add whole numbers, but I do not know what a 'whole' means in 1/3 or why the bottom number matters.
openPrerequisites: interpret denominator as size/count of equal parts
pathways.firstDecisionTarget: Establish the chosen whole and equal-sized fractional unit in concrete terms; check that the learner follows before teaching a common denominator.
pathways.avoidableCostRisk: Repeatedly using inaccessible words such as whole or unit instead of repairing their meaning.

pathways.authoredLearnerEvidence: I know a fraction is equal parts of a whole, but I thought 1/3 + 1/4 = 2/7. I do not know how to make the pieces the same size.
evidencedKnownConcepts: interpret denominator as size/count of equal parts
pathways.firstDecisionTarget: Preserve knowledge about equal-sized parts; connect equivalence to common units and offer one executable next step.
pathways.avoidableCostRisk: Restarting the entire explanation of wholes and equal parts instead of addressing equivalent fractions.

pathways.authoredLearnerEvidence: I converted 1/3 and 1/4 into twelfths: 4/12 + 3/12 = 7/12. Can I try a more difficult one rather than review the basics?
evidencedKnownConcepts: interpret denominator as size/count of equal parts
add quantities in the same units
pathways.firstDecisionTarget: Confirm the visible work briefly and offer an independent transfer challenge; do not force the full foundation lecture.
pathways.avoidableCostRisk: Over-scaffolding and delaying new, independently attempted challenges after sufficient local evidence.

tutorObservable: whether the learner receives an executable next step
whether hints are escalated or faded using subsequent evidence
observationPlan.feedbackPolicy: Do not score an independent checkpoint if tutoring or hints were supplied during it; preserve that event as a protocol deviation.
